name: Cassava leaf stew
subtitle: Cassava leaf stew is a Sierra Leonean stew of pounded or blended cassava leaves cooked with oil, onions, meat or fish and, in many versions, peanut butter.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: A comfort food for many Sierra Leoneans, also popular across West Africa with slight variations.

facts.label: Main ingredients
facts.value: In Maria Bradford's description, pounded and shredded cassava leaves are cooked in coconut oil with onions, ogiri (fermented oil seeds), butter beans, peanut butter and a little okra, and eaten with chilli.

facts.label: Main ingredient
facts.value: Palm oil is the foundation of many stews in Sierra Leone, and it turns deep brown when mixed with cassava leaves.

facts.label: Where
facts.value: The cassava leaf and other West African staples cross national as well as provincial boundaries.

facts.label: Nutrition
facts.value: Sierra Leone's dietary guidelines list cassava leaves among commonly available dark green leafy vegetables rich in vitamin A.

parts.text: Cassava leaf stew is a Sierra Leonean stew of pounded or blended cassava leaves cooked with oil, onions, meat or fish and, in many versions, peanut butter. Palm oil is the base of many stews in Sierra Leone and turns deep brown when it meets the leaves; Maria Bradford's version uses coconut oil, ogiri, butter beans and a little okra. The national tourist board calls it a comfort food for many Sierra Leoneans and notes that it is cooked across West Africa with variations.
It is served over white rice and eaten with chilli; Freetown eateries serve it alongside groundnut stew.
